p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The vastness of the universe, with its billions of galaxies and innumerable stars, fuels ongoing speculation about the existence of extraterrestrial life. Astrobiology, the scientific discipline dedicated to studying life's potential beyond Earth, integrates astronomy, biology, and geology to explore this profound question. Despite decades of observation and advances in space exploration, definitive evidence of alien life remains elusive. However, discoveries of extremophiles on Earth — organisms thriving in conditions previously thought uninhabitable — expand the conceivable habitats where life might exist elsewhere. Furthermore, the identification of exoplanets within habitable zones around distant stars has intensified the search for biosignatures indicative of life. The Fermi Paradox, highlighting the contradiction between the high probability of extraterrestrial civilizations and the lack of contact, emphasizes the complexities of this quest. Reasons for the paradox range from the rarity of advanced life to limits on interstellar communication or travel. As technology progresses, initiatives like the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence (SETI) and upcoming space missions aim to unravel these cosmic mysteries, underscoring humanity's profound curiosity about our place in the cosmos.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: The traditional linear economic model—predicated on an extractive "take-make-waste" philosophy—has driven global ecosystems to the brink of a waste crisis, choked by plastic pollution and hazardous electronic waste. For decades, municipal waste management relied on a "downstream" approach, focusing on expanding landfills and building energy-intensive incinerators. These methods merely conceal or transform garbage rather than eliminating its volume, releasing toxic leachates and greenhouse gases back into the environment. Transitioning to a circular economy requires an absolute "upstream" transformation, where products are intentionally engineered from inception for durability, modular disassembly, and complete material recovery. This shift demands strict Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations that legally bind corporations to internalize the end-of-life environmental costs of their goods. Furthermore, upgrading the waste sector requires formalizing and protecting the informal recycling networks that handle waste collection in developing countries. Ultimately, a circular economy is not a simple community recycling initiative; it requires a complete decoupling of industrial economic growth from finite resource consumption.

questions.q: What is the primary focus of astrobiology as mentioned in the passage?
opts: Studying life's potential beyond Earth by combining several sciences
Cataloguing planets in the solar system
questions.why: Detail: it 'integrates astronomy, biology, and geology'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Assistant cum Photographer), Sep 2025.

questions.q: How do extremophiles discovered on Earth contribute to the search for extraterrestrial life?
opts: They prove aliens exist on Earth
They show life can exist in harsh environments
questions.why: Inference: they 'expand the conceivable habitats where life might exist'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Assistant cum Photographer), Sep 2025.

questions.q: What does the Fermi Paradox highlight?
opts: The abundance of alien signals detected
The contradiction between probable alien civilizations and the lack of contact
questions.why: Detail: defined in the sixth sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Assistant cum Photographer), Sep 2025.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT cited as a possible reason for the Fermi Paradox?
questions.why: NOT question: the other three are listed. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Assistant cum Photographer), Sep 2025.

questions.q: What future efforts are described as aiming to unravel the mysteries of alien life?
opts: Initiatives like SETI and upcoming space missions
questions.why: Detail: the last sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Assistant cum Photographer), Sep 2025.

questions.q: The primary flaw the author identifies in the "downstream" approach to waste is that it:
opts: Conceals or transforms waste rather than reducing its volume.
Forces economies to stop making electronic goods.
Depends too much on EPR regulations.
Relies too heavily on informal recyclers.
questions.why: Detail: 'merely conceal or transform garbage rather than eliminating its volume'. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: A "circular economy", as described in the passage, fundamentally requires:
opts: Engineering products from the start for durability, easy disassembly and recycling.
Shifting all recovery costs to consumers.
Moving all manufacturing to waste-to-energy incinerators.
questions.why: Detail: the 'upstream' transformation in the fourth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: What does Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) legally require corporations to do?
opts: Pay the state to manage informal waste workers.
Bear the end-of-life environmental costs of their products.
questions.why: Detail: 'internalize the end-of-life environmental costs of their goods'. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The passage says waste reform in developing countries must include:
opts: Formalizing and protecting informal waste workers.
questions.why: Detail: the sixth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The ultimate goal of a circular economy, according to the final sentence, is to:
opts: Ensure economic growth no longer depends on consuming finite resources.
questions.why: Main idea: 'decoupling of industrial economic growth from finite resource consumption'. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “They say that he is honest.”
opts: It is said him to be honest.
He was said to be honest.
He is said to be honest.
questions.why: Report-verb passive: subject + is said + to-infinitive. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “Someone has stolen my bag.”
questions.why: Present perfect passive: has been + past participle; drop 'someone'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: He said, “I am tired.”
opts: He said that he was tired.
He said that I was tired.
He said that he is tired.
He said that he had been tired yesterday.
questions.why: Reporting verb in the past: am → was; I → he. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: She asked me, “Where do you live?”
opts: She asked me where I lived.
She asked me where did I live.
She asked me where do I live.
She asked me that where I lived.
questions.why: Reported questions use statement word order and no 'that'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Identify the error: “One of my friend has joined the health department.”
questions.why: 'One of' takes a plural noun: 'one of my friends'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Dudhsagar waterfalls are on which river?
questions.why: On the Goa–Karnataka border.

questions.q: Silent Valley National Park is in:

questions.q: Kaziranga National Park, famous for the one-horned rhinoceros, is in:
questions.why: A UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.q: The Battle of Plassey was fought in:
questions.why: Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah.

questions.q: The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana, which completed six years in September 2026, is for the:
Glasgow, host of the 2026 Commonwealth Games, is in:

questions.q: World Teachers' Day is observed on:
questions.why: India's own Teachers' Day is 5 September.

questions.q: Indian Air Force Day is observed on:
questions.why: The IAF was founded on 8 October 1932.

questions.q: The SI unit of electrical resistance is the:
questions.why: Static science.

questions.q: The International Day of the Girl Child is observed on:
questions.why: National Girl Child Day in India is 24 January.

questions.q: D and E are a married couple, and D is the husband. A and B are their children. A is B's brother, and B is the mother of C. How is C related to E?
questions.why: E is the mother of B, and B is the mother of C, so C is E's grandchild. Nothing in the statement tells us whether C is male or female.

questions.q: Mamlatdar is to Taluka as Collector is to:
questions.why: A Mamlatdar heads the revenue administration of a taluka; a Collector heads that of a district.

questions.q: If ROAD is written as URDG in a certain code, how is FORT written?
questions.why: Each letter moves three places forward: F-I, O-R, R-U, T-W.

questions.q: If TABLE is written as UBCMF in a certain code, how is CHAIR written?
questions.why: Each letter moves one place forward: C-D, H-I, A-B, I-J, R-S.

questions.q: If A = 2, B = 4, C = 6 and so on, what is the value of G + O + A?
Which letter is eighth to the right of the fifteenth letter from the left in the English alphabet?
questions.why: The fifteenth letter is O. Eight places on is the twenty-third letter, W.

questions.q: Find the next term in the series: AZ, BY, CX, DW, ?
questions.why: The first letter moves forward and the second moves backward: E and V.

questions.q: Konkani is to Goa as Malayalam is to:
questions.why: Konkani is the official language of Goa; Malayalam of Kerala.

questions.q: ACE is to BDF as GIK is to:
questions.why: Each letter moves one place forward: G-H, I-J, K-L.

questions.q: If OFFICE is written as PGGJDF in a certain code, how is TALUKA written?
questions.why: Each letter moves one place forward: T-U, A-B, L-M, U-V, K-L, A-B.

questions.q: Which miasm has the itch eruption as its primary manifestation?
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Psora is the chronic miasm whose primary outward sign is the itch (scabies-like) eruption.

questions.q: The palliative method that treats with an opposite (contraria contrariis) is called:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Hahnemann discussed it in §§57–60; relief is followed by worsening.

questions.q: Warts and fig-warts, catarrhal discharges and a tendency to overgrowths are clinical features of which miasm?
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Sycosis: infiltration and overgrowth (warts, condylomata).

questions.q: Which remedy is regarded as the chronic of Pulsatilla?
questions.why: Silicea is the chronic of Pulsatilla. The two share a yielding, mild temperament and similar discharges.

questions.q: Profuse, watery, painless diarrhoea with marked prostration, cold sweat on the forehead and collapse calls for:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Veratrum album: cold sweat on the forehead, collapse.

questions.q: Ill effects of grief with sighing, a lump in the throat, contradictory symptoms and aversion to consolation suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Ignatia: paradoxical symptoms, acute grief.

questions.q: Complaints from exposure to damp cold, especially when hot days are followed by cold nights, call for:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Dulcamara: diarrhoea, rheumatism and skin complaints from damp cold.

questions.q: The abbreviation 'a.c.' on a prescription means:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Ante cibum; p.c. = after meals.

questions.q: The vehicle used to prepare mother tinctures from fresh plants is:
opts: Purified alcohol (strong alcohol or dispensing alcohol)
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Alcohol of the strength laid down in the HPI.

questions.q: In Kent's Repertory, remedies of the highest grade are printed in:
questions.why: Three grades: bold (3 marks), italics (2), roman (1).

questions.q: The process of choosing the most similar remedy using a repertory is called:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. It narrows the remedies to a few for study in the materia medica.

questions.q: Foot drop follows injury to the:
questions.why: It winds around the neck of the fibula and supplies the dorsiflexors.

questions.q: The hormone that regulates blood calcium and is secreted by the parathyroid glands is:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. It raises serum calcium.

questions.q: The first cells to arrive at a site of acute inflammation are usually:
questions.why: Neutrophils dominate the first 6–24 hours.

questions.q: Negri bodies are seen in:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. In the hippocampus and Purkinje cells.

questions.q: Central chest pain on exertion, relieved by rest within a few minutes, is typical of:
questions.why: MI pain lasts longer than 20 minutes and is not relieved by rest.

questions.q: Urticaria with burning, stinging wheals, worse from heat and better from cold applications, calls for:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Apis: oedematous, stinging wheals, thirstless, better from cold.

questions.q: The usual HbA1c target for most adults with diabetes is below:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Targets are individualised; 7% suits most adults.

questions.q: Oligomenorrhoea, hirsutism, acne and multiple small ovarian follicles on ultrasound suggest:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Rotterdam criteria: two of anovulation, hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovaries.

questions.q: The commonest benign tumour of the uterus, a frequent cause of heavy menstrual bleeding, is the:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Fibroids are smooth-muscle tumours; they cause menorrhagia and infertility.

questions.q: Punctured wounds that feel cold to touch yet are better from cold applications call for:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Ledum: puncture wounds, insect bites; cold yet better by cold.

questions.q: Fractures that are slow to unite, with pricking pain at the site, are helped by:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Symphytum ('knitbone') promotes union of fractures.

questions.q: In medical ethics, 'informed consent' requires that the patient:
opts: understands the nature, risks and alternatives of the procedure and agrees voluntarily
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Consent must be informed, voluntary and given by a competent person.

questions.q: A registered medical practitioner who fails to exercise reasonable skill and care, causing harm, may be liable for:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Duty, breach, damage and causation.

questions.q: The measure of central tendency most affected by extreme values is the:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. The median is resistant to outliers.
